title: Cap. X Arg. X close: reprobates lack saving grace because they are not what God requires — that itself proves antecedent rejection; Col. i. 12; no middle between election and reprobation
pass_a_gloss: Finally, what Corvinus says, that saving grace is not given unto the reprobate because by their own fault they are not such as God prerequires, this itself argues that they were antecedently rejected or passed by: For God has decreed to make all the elect such as he himself is wont to prerequire unto taking hold of grace and glory, Coloss. i. 12. Those therefore whom he has not made such, them he has not elected; and because no middle is given between election and reprobation, the same he has reprobated. After so many windings and turns we must therefore return hither, that those unto whom the grace of faith, repentance and perseverance has not been given, we acknowledge as passed by in the ordination unto everlasting life; just as on the contrary we confess as elect those unto whom these things have been prepared and given. And as certain ones were mercifully elected unto these goods before foresight of the same as existing in them, so certain ones were passed by, and by no means predestinated unto receiving such things, before they were foreseen as finally lacking such goods.
pass_b_english: Finally Corvinus says saving grace is not given to the reprobate because by their fault they are not what God prerequires—and that itself proves they were antecedently rejected or passed by. For God has decreed to make all the elect such as he is wont to prerequire for laying hold of grace and glory (Col. i. 12). Those he has not made such, he has not elected; and since there is no middle between election and reprobation, he has reprobated them. After so many twists we must come back here: those not given the grace of faith, repentance, and perseverance we acknowledge as passed by in the ordination to everlasting life; those for whom these were prepared and given we confess as elect. And as some were mercifully elected to these goods before foresight of them as existing in them, so some were passed by and not predestined to receive such things before they were foreseen as finally lacking them.
source_text: Denique, quod dicit Corvinus, reprobis non dari gratiam salutiferam, quia sua culpa tales non sunt, quales Deus praerequirit, hoc ipsum arguit eos fuisse antecedenter rejectos sive praeteritos: Nam Deus decrevit omnes electos tales efficere, quales ad capessendum gratiam et gloriam ipse solet praerequirere, Coloss. i. 12. Quos ergo tales non effecit, eos non elegit; et quia non datur medium inter electionem et reprobationem, eosdem reprobavit. Post tot anfractus et gyros huc itaque redeamus oportet, ut quibus gratia fidei, poenitentiae et perseverantiae data non fuerit, eos in ordinatione ad vitam aeternam praeteritos agnoscamus; sicut e contra, eos quibus haec fuerunt praeparata et donata, electos confiteamur. Atque ut quidam electi fuerunt misericorditer ad haec bona ante praevisionem eorundem ut in illis existentium, ita quidam praeteriti fuerunt, et ad talia accipienda haud praedestinati, antequam praeviderentur ut talibus bonis finaliter carentes.
